what: Baxter makes hospital basics: intravenous fluids and the pumps that deliver them, dialysis equipment and solutions, surgical sealants and hospital beds.
customers: Hospitals and dialysis clinics worldwide, plus patients on home dialysis.
money: IV solutions, infusion pumps and surgical products
hospital beds, monitoring and connected care
moat: Intravenous solutions are a low-price, high-volume product very few companies make, and hospitals cannot run without them: Baxter is one of a handful of suppliers in the United States.
risks: A reported net loss of $723M, after write-downs and the separation of the kidney care business
Hurricane damage to its North Carolina IV fluid plant in 2024 caused a national shortage and lost sales
opportunities: $1.1B of free cash flow against a $13.1B market value, under 12 times cash flow
Spinning off kidney care leaves a simpler company focused on hospital products
watch: Infusion pump sales and the recovery in IV solutions supply.
